markdown_report:
**Selected direction: supervision-controlled prefix truncation in NextItNet.** At 10% progress, retain this feasible intervention, but distinguish augmentation effects from changes in supervision.

Three starting insights motivate it. First, positive sampled-negative margins coexist with weak training-prefix catalog ranking. Different examples and candidate universes prevent attributing this discrepancy to sampling failure. Second, terminal-preserving permutations worsen ranks on measured prefixes. This supports order sensitivity; sparse replacement support leaves recency conclusions unresolved. Third, qualitative feedback favors specific recent context. Histories do not establish present intent, ownership, or compatibility, so truncation remains a generalization hypothesis.

Three literature insights refine the design. NextItNet combines causal convolutions with autoregressive supervision [1]; changing endpoints changes examples, whereas shortening context before the same target preserves adjacency. Effective receptive fields can differ from theoretical bounds [2]; structurally unreachable edits provide conditional null controls. CL4SRec establishes cropping precedent [4], while intervention research emphasizes corruption and measurement choices [3]. Neither establishes benefits from this controlled NextItNet experiment.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Main unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Context regularization | Remove older prefix items | Does restricted context improve validation? |
| Supervision control | Match targets, negatives and weights | Is improvement attributable to context? |
| Measurement calibration | Preserve positions; test unreachable edits | Does the probe measure the intended change? |

Three candidate algorithms, scored originality/potential/difficulty:

- **Matched truncation: 3/6/4.** Originality: careful causal-context control (+), established cropping precedent (−). Potential: interpretable training comparison (+), may discard useful history (−). Difficulty: unchanged backbone (+), supervision and random-stream matching require care (−). Builds on [1,2,4].
- **Suffix-length curriculum: 3/6/4.** Originality: temporal schedule (+), familiar curriculum design (−). Potential: gradual adaptation (+), adds schedule sensitivity (−). Difficulty: simple scheduler (+), harder attribution (−). Builds on [1,2].
- **Paired suffix consistency: 4/6/5.** Originality: shared-network context regularization (+), established consistency/contrastive precedent (−). Potential: stable representations (+), may suppress useful context dependence (−). Difficulty: one checkpoint (+), extra computation and loss tuning (−). Inspired by [3,4].

Choose **matched truncation**. Compare matched full context, stochastic suffix retention, and a deterministic half-context control. Treatment retains full context with probability 0.5; otherwise sample suffix length uniformly from ceil(n/2) through n. Keep targets, negatives, tensor width, retained positions, loss weights and updates identical. Endpoint-only supervision is shared across these conditions; comparison with the dense baseline alone cannot isolate cropping.

Train conditions independently; deploy one NextItNet checkpoint per category with full-context inference. Preregister checkpoint and stopping rules. Report every category/macro HR@10, paired wins/losses and conditional user-bootstrap intervals. The pinned 100-candidate metric is not full-catalog HR@10 [5]; adaptive validation reuse remains selection-biased [7]. No improvement has been measured.

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic removal of older prefix items in the supplied corrected NextItNet against matched full-context and deterministic half-context controls. Preserve the ordered supervised target stream, negative IDs, target weights, loss normalization and optimizer updates. Each condition trains exactly one independent model per category and serves exactly one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The supplied diagnostics support sensitivity to history ordering but do not establish that recent context is underweighted or that negative sampling fails. A controlled truncation experiment tests whether shortening accessible context improves pinned validation ranking. A fixed-length control helps distinguish random context variation from a deterministic preference for shorter histories. This limited intervention suits 10% research progress, although basic cropping has low novelty and matched supervision is the principal methodological contribution.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the corrected NextItNet backbone, architecture settings, optimizer, objective and baseline inference window for the initial experiment. Preregister three separate conditions: matched_full, matched_random_suffix and matched_half_suffix. Never combine their scores, parameters or checkpoints. Each condition starts from the host-supplied corrected cold start; do not inspect other trials or reuse their trained weights. The deterministic half-context condition is a control, not an additional prediction component. Retain suffix-length curriculum and paired suffix consistency as later hypotheses rather than adding their schedules or losses to this initial intervention.

Use the family-specific sample_batch to obtain aligned training examples. Select one valid supervised endpoint per sampled row using a deterministic training-only schedule shared across conditions. One reproducible schedule selects valid_position[(epoch * 200 + batch_index + row_index) % valid_position_count], ordering valid positions by input index. A valid endpoint has nonzero sequence, positive and negative IDs under the supplied alignment contract. Preserve the original sampler and verify that positive at endpoint j is its immediate next training interaction, not a later terminal label. If sampling performs preprocessing or random endpoint selection internally, retain those semantics and record the resulting example IDs. Inputs contain only interactions through the chosen endpoint; exclude the target occurrence and subsequent interactions. Earlier occurrences of the target item may remain legitimate history.

This endpoint-only supervision deliberately differs from the dense baseline. All three matched conditions must share it, including every target's realized multiplicity and weight. A difference between matched_random_suffix and matched_full estimates the effect of that context policy under endpoint-only supervision; it does not establish the same effect under dense supervision. Report the corrected dense baseline separately only when its result is legitimately supplied or independently trained within budget. Do not read another trial to obtain it. Preserving dense supervision would require separate causal prefix examples for every original target, or another construction proven to preserve every target's accessible context and loss weight. That extension increases computation and code difficulty and is deferred.

Construct a fixed-width endpoint prefix by replacing positions after the endpoint with PAD without shifting earlier tokens. At training time gather the feature at the endpoint's actual maximum nonpadding input index. If the supplied implementation internally slices a window or generates position IDs, ensure the endpoint is represented and its feature index is mapped correctly. Do not assume that an endpoint inside a long tensor is encoded identically by an implementation that processes only a terminal raw window. If necessary, construct each endpoint example through the baseline's existing fixed-width history builder, identically across conditions, before applying suffix removal. Preserve retained positions and positional IDs within that shared representation.

For n available input items within that representation, matched_full retains n. matched_half_suffix retains ceil(n/2). matched_random_suffix retains n with probability 0.5; otherwise it samples k uniformly from ceil(n/2) through n, inclusive, and replaces the oldest n-k occupied positions with PAD. Its actual full-context probability is 0.5 + 0.5/(n-ceil(n/2)+1); record this rather than describing it as exactly 0.5. Rows with one input item remain unchanged. Retain the terminal item, fixed tensor width, retained-item positions and baseline positional IDs. Do not introduce an untrained mask token or an arbitrary interior crop. The half-context control is a simple shorter-context comparator; it does not match the random policy's mean retained length or isolate every consequence of randomness.

Sample negatives using the original training-history exclusion policy, independent of the retained suffix. Do not make removed historical items newly eligible negatives. Keep the exact sampled negative IDs and multiplicities identical across matched conditions. Preserve the baseline positive/negative objective, its external coefficients and negative reduction. Normalize over the same valid supervised examples with the same target weights, excluding PAD. Use one context view per target per update. If multiple views are later added, average losses within target before averaging targets and treat that as a separate experiment. Handle invalid or empty rows identically and record exclusions; do not silently change batch denominators.

Match initialization, logical batch composition, optimizer, gradient accumulation, clipping, learning-rate schedule by optimizer-update count, and total updates. Use separate generators for augmentation, training-example sampling and negatives, and retain the baseline dropout stream. Merely giving global RNGs the same initial seed is insufficient if augmentation changes their consumption. Use a CPU torch.Generator seeded 42 for augmentation; keep preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Serialize generator settings and schedules beneath the current trial directory, or deterministically regenerate them within each condition without accessing another trial. Verify equality of the independently generated ordered endpoint/negative streams using hashes and counts.

Keep at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Preregister the common epoch cap, checkpoint rule, validation-query schedule and stopping rule before obtaining new scores. For the primary controlled comparison, use the same fixed training horizon and its final checkpoint across conditions; do not introduce condition-specific early stopping. If the host mandates another checkpoint-selection rule, record and apply that same rule to all conditions, and acknowledge that selected checkpoints can differ in training exposure. Run only complete, preregistered conditions affordable within the remaining shared budget; report omitted controls explicitly. Do not infer a runtime from the supplied diagnostic timings. Failed runs, debugging and diagnostics consume the 43,200 GPU-second budget.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, their routing and original splits. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. At inference use the baseline full context without stochastic cropping. Gather the maximum index whose item ID is nonzero, never count-1, and preserve the supplied empty-history policy. Keep the trained class, checkpoint configuration and embedded predictor writer consistent. Each category loads exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint; no averaging, score fusion, transition/popularity predictor, pretrained weights or external data are introduced.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), every ModelView interface and the B x L loader contract. Preserve view.model as the actual trained nn.Module, log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Dense training-position margin probes may remain, but label them as diagnostic measurements rather than the endpoint-only optimization objective. Return measured metrics and metric_definitions; unavailable or empty quantities should be null with a reason rather than an apparently measured zero. Preserve RNG states and individual module modes when running frozen-model diagnostics.

Before training, check synthetic mixed-length examples for endpoint/label adjacency, identical negatives and weights across conditions, unchanged retained positions, correct final-nonpadding readout, and absence of future-token influence. Verify that augmentation draws do not advance sampling or dropout RNG streams. Verify loss reductions on unequal-length rows. Derive convolutional reachability from the actual backbone, counting every temporal convolution: for stride-one convolutions, R = 1 + sum_l((k_l-1)*d_l). This width alone is not a proof of the full dependency graph. Edits outside it are null controls only when there are no other information paths, positional changes, temporal normalization/pooling or altered boundaries. Per-position channel LayerNorm alone does not mix time positions. Report realized retained lengths and the proportion of crops intersecting each endpoint's structural receptive field; no-op crops can dilute the treatment. Do not infer learned influence from structural accessibility.

The primary planned contrast is matched_random_suffix minus matched_full in pinned macro validation HR@10. Secondary contrasts compare matched_half_suffix with matched_full and matched_random_suffix with matched_half_suffix. The host retains its fixed 200 users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42 and equal category weights. Do not modify or reproduce an alternative authoritative evaluator. With this design, one additional hit changes a category by 0.5 percentage points and the four-category macro by 0.125 percentage points. This candidate-set metric does not establish full-catalog HR@10 or recommendation usefulness.

Report every condition's category and macro result, differences in percentage points, validation-query count and prior adaptive search history. If the host exposes paired per-user hits, retain them and report wins/losses for each contrast. Use 10,000 bootstrap replicates with bootstrap seed 42: independently resample 200 users with replacement within each category, reuse those indices across conditions and contrasts, and recompute equally weighted macro differences. For three planned contrasts, report Bonferroni-adjusted percentile intervals using quantiles 0.05/(2*3) and 1-0.05/(2*3), an approximate simultaneous 95% procedure. Record the method and sparse/discrete-data limitations. If only aggregate scores are available, mark paired intervals and discordant counts unavailable rather than modifying the host evaluator. These intervals condition on trained models and fixed candidates; they omit training-seed variability, candidate-sampling variability, population shift and adaptive model selection. Winner-only intervals do not correct validation selection bias, and preregistration now cannot erase previous validation reuse. Treat adaptively selected findings as exploratory; reserve held-out generalization assessment for the host's untouched final evaluation.

Monitor retained-length, original-history-length and training-item-frequency strata using training data; obtain validation strata only through host-exposed permitted records. Shortened context can encourage last-item or popularity shortcuts, and may remove useful long-range dependencies. Order sensitivity or improved sampled margins cannot establish current intent or functional compatibility. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category, separately from the pinned validation candidate task. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; do not invent reviews, ratings, item categories/prices/stores, ownership, compatibility evidence or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch


def retain_suffix(sequence, mode, augmentation_rng):
    """Fixed-width endpoint prefixes; preserve retained positions and terminal item."""
    result = sequence.clone()
    for row in range(sequence.shape[0]):
        occupied = torch.nonzero(sequence[row] != 0, as_tuple=False).flatten()
        n = occupied.numel()
        if n <= 1 or mode == 'matched_full':
            continue
        minimum = (n + 1) // 2
        if mode == 'matched_half_suffix':
            retained = minimum
        elif mode == 'matched_random_suffix':
            if torch.rand((), generator=augmentation_rng).item() < 0.5:
                retained = n
            else:
                retained = torch.randint(
                    minimum, n + 1, (), generator=augmentation_rng).item()
        else:
            raise ValueError(mode)
        result[row, occupied[:n - retained]] = 0
    return result


def final_nonpadding(features, sequence):
    # Requires features to align with these input positions, as verified in integration.
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    final = positions.expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(sequence == 0, -1).amax(dim=1)
    valid = final >= 0
    return features[valid, final[valid]], valid


# Integration outline: hooks below must use the supplied corrected baseline.
# No filesystem inspection, training or validation has been performed here.
# Preregister horizon, query/checkpoint rules, contrasts and budget before execution.
for condition in PREREGISTERED_AFFORDABLE_CONDITIONS:
    for category in FOUR_FIXED_CATEGORIES:
        seed_training(42)
        model, optimizer = corrected_nextitnet_cold_start(category)
        # Separate streams reproduce identical examples/negatives in every condition.
        sampler = make_family_sampler_with_separate_rng(seed=42)
        augmentation_rng = torch.Generator(device='cpu').manual_seed(42)
        stream_digest = new_stream_digest()
        for epoch in range(PREREGISTERED_COMMON_EPOCHS):  # <= 200
            for batch_index in range(200):
                batch = sampler.sample_batch()
                # Select valid endpoint j by the fixed row/epoch/batch schedule.
                # Build its causal baseline representation ending at x[j],
                # with target x[j+1], unchanged negative IDs and target weights.
                sequence, positive, negative, weights, example_ids = (
                    build_verified_endpoint_examples(batch, epoch, batch_index))
                update_digest(stream_digest, example_ids, positive, negative, weights)
                sequence = retain_suffix(sequence, condition, augmentation_rng)
                features, valid = final_nonpadding(model.log2feats(sequence), sequence)
                # Preserve objective coefficients and within-target negative reduction.
                # Reduce over the identical supervised-example weights in all arms.
                loss = unchanged_weighted_endpoint_loss(
                    model.predict_score(features, positive[valid]),
                    model.predict_score(features, negative[valid]), weights[valid])
                unchanged_optimizer_update(optimizer, loss)
        save_trial_local_stream_hash_and_realized_crop_counts(stream_digest)
        save_one_category_checkpoint_and_consistent_predictor(model)
# Each condition serves one checkpoint/category, with original full-context inference.
# Host independently evaluates unchanged users/candidates and equal-category macro HR@10.
# Report every result and all validation queries; never combine conditions' predictions.
# If host provides paired hits: compute wins/losses and stratified paired bootstrap
# differences with 10,000 replicates, seed 42, and the prespecified multiplicity rule.
# Otherwise mark these paired summaries unavailable; do not alter the evaluator.

originality.positive: Explicitly matches endpoints, negatives, positional representation, target weights and optimizer exposure to test a context policy within NextItNet.
originality.negative: Cropping is established in sequential recommendation; experimental rigor rather than a new modeling principle supplies most of the contribution.

future_potential.positive: Provides a practical foundation for studying accessible context and autoregressive supervision, with fixed-context controls and transparent validation accounting.
future_potential.negative: Endpoint-only results may not transfer to dense supervision, and neither diagnostic sensitivity nor cropping precedent establishes validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone and inference architecture, requiring primarily training-example construction and input augmentation.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable endpoint mapping, independent RNG streams, matched supervision and host-dependent paired reporting exceed a simple crop implementation; dense matching would be harder.

related_work.title: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: [1] Introduces NextItNet's causal dilated convolutions and autoregressive next-item supervision.
Supports distinguishing suffix shortening before an unchanged target from selecting an earlier endpoint with a different target.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed matched suffix augmentation improves this benchmark.
The actual supplied implementation determines positional handling, feature alignment and dependency paths.

related_work.title: Understanding the Effective Receptive Field in Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
contributions: [2] Distinguishes effective influence from theoretical convolutional receptive-field extent.
Motivates separating structural accessibility, no-op context edits and measured sensitivity.
limitations: Provides general CNN evidence rather than NextItNet-specific recommendation results.
Does not establish that older interactions are unhelpful or that truncation improves ranking.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: [3] Examines how corruption and measurement choices affect intervention conclusions.
Motivates explicit controls and cautious interpretation of sequence perturbations.
limitations: Studies language models; transfer to recommendation requires validation.
Does not establish benefits from suffix consistency or truncation in NextItNet.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: [4] Introduces cropping, masking and reordering views with a shared sequential encoder and contrastive training.
Provides cropping and augmentation-only ablation precedent, reducing the novelty attributable to cropping itself.
limitations: Randomly located subsequence cropping differs from retaining a suffix immediately before an unchanged target.
The cited ablation does not document matching all target multiplicities, supervised positions, negative draws, loss denominators and optimizer updates.
Its reported results do not establish effects for this corrected NextItNet and pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: [5] Analyzes differences between sampled-candidate and full-catalog recommendation metrics.
Shows why sampled metrics can yield different model rankings, including in expectation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the required pinned benchmark as the task's selection objective.
Does not supply a task-specific conversion from 100-candidate HR@10 to full-catalog HR@10.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: [6] Documents bootstrap confidence intervals and paired resampling.
Supports preserving paired observations when estimating differences between conditions.
limitations: The four-category stratified macro requires an explicitly implemented resampling design.
Bootstrap intervals do not automatically address adaptive selection, sparse discrete hits, candidate uncertainty or training-seed variability.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: [7] Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting optimistic performance estimates.
Motivates recording adaptive validation reuse and reserving generalization assessment for untouched evaluation.
limitations: Preregistration of subsequent comparisons cannot undo earlier adaptive reuse.
Neither paired bootstrap intervals nor adjustment for three planned contrasts corrects an unrestricted prior search.
